newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Suharto arrives in Cambodia for three-day visit.
newsitem.headline: Suharto arrives in Cambodia for three-day visit.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto arrived in Cambodia on Monday, his first stop on a visit to three countries seeking to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional grouping.

Suharto, who last visited Cambodia in 1968, was met on arrival by King Norodom Sihanouk, co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and other senior officials and diplomats as well as colourfully dressed ethnic minorities and children.
A delegation of more than 50 government and business officials, including Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, accompanied him.
Suharto was to proceed to the palace for a formal mid-day meeting with Sihanouk, his long-time friend.

During his three-day visit, he was due to hold formal talks with Ranariddh and Hun Sen and to witness the signing of several bilateral agreements, including a trade agreement and a pact on oil and gas exploration and development.
Suharto will also visit Burma and Laos during his trip.
The three countries hope to join ASEAN this year as the club celebrates its 30th anniversary.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
